A $15,250 bond was set, and reports indicate Morgan was released from jail roughly three hours later.
He was charged with three felony counts of reckless endangerment with a deadly weapon
and one misdemeanor count of disorderly conduct.
Tennessee Law List Classy felony sentences at a minimum of one year in prison,
serious charges that could heavily affect his music career.
Eight months later in December of 2024, Morgan made a plea deal and was found guilty
on what appears to be two reduced misdemeanor counts of reckless endangerment, all other charges
were dropped. He was ordered to spend seven days at a DUI education center and was given two years
of probation. His fines amounted to $350 plus court fees. When his sentence is complete, his charges
are set to be expunged from the record. Shortly after his plea agreement, the Nashville
Metro Council approved his bar's sign proposal, adding to the list of neon signs that illuminate
the strip. Since this incident, Morgan has stayed out of legal trouble. Assuming his probation
began at sentencing, it will end in December of 2026.
